property_summary: After a deposit, the contract's ETH balance increases by exactly the deposited amount.
After deposit, the depositor's balance as reported by balances[msg.sender] must equal the sum of the previous balance plus the deposited amount.
After Deposit, the depositor's balance must equal the previous balance plus the deposited amount.
After a deposit, the sender's balance must equal the sent amount (with no prior balance); the bug never updates balances so the balance remains 0.

After a successful Collect, the contract's total balance of all recorded deposits (sum of balances) must equal the contract's Ether balance minus any uncollected initial ether; the bug fails to update balances on Deposit, so total recorded becomes less than actual Ether held when a subsequent Collect sends out ether.

After any sequence of deposits and a successful collect of amount _am from the caller, the caller's balance must decrease by exactly _am; the bug never increases balances during deposit, so after a deposit followed by a collect, the caller's balance decreases from its pre-deposit value, which differs from the correct contract's behaviour.

When a depositor later collects part of their balance, the remaining balance of any non‑collecting prior depositor must stay unchanged; the bug never records deposits, so a subsequent collect can cause another user’s balance to be incorrectly reduced (or left at zero when it should be unaffected).
After a deposit, the sum of all recorded balances must equal the total Ether received via Deposit; the bug fails to update balances, so sum of balances remains less than total Ether deposited.
After any sequence of calls, the balance of the caller of Deposit must increase by at least the deposited amount (subject to overflow), but in the mutant the caller's balance remains unchanged.

property_summary: After any sequence of operations involving Collect, the sum of all balances in the mapping must equal the total Ether received by the contract minus the total Ether sent out; the bug increments a fixed address instead of the caller, so a Collect by a user with sufficient balance will reduce their own balance but the fixed address's balance remains as if the deposit went to it, breaking the invariant.

After a deposit and subsequent Collect, the caller's balance correctly reflects their own net deposits minus withdrawals, ensuring no user's balance is credited to another fixed address; the bug breaks this by crediting deposits to address(0), so when the original caller collects, their balance can go negative or carry the wrong value while address(0) holds the deposit.

After any sequence of deposits and collects, the balance of any address must be bounded by that address's own net deposits minus its own net successful collects; the bug credits deposits to address(0) so a collect by address(0) (when it has no deposits of its own) can succeed using funds that were meant for other users, breaking the per-address isolation invariant.

After any sequence of operations, the balance of the caller of Deposit() must equal the sum of their own deposits minus their own successful collects; the bug credits deposits to address(0) instead of the caller, so after a Deposit by Alice and a Collect by Alice, Alice's balance will be less than her net contribution while address(0) holds the miscredited funds.

The caller's balance after deposition must equal their prior balance plus the deposited amount; the bug credits address(0) instead of the caller, so after any call to Deposit the caller's balance remains unchanged while address(0) increases.
